newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty stabilises at one pct above parity.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty stabilises at one pct above parity.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilised at around one percent above the trading band centre after large exporters' currency sell orders and ensuing speculation shook it out of its recent bearish mood, dealers said.

They said early exporters' sales totalling more than $50 million attracted speculative currency position shorteneing from banks and pushed the zloty to highs of 1.27/1.17 percent above parity but subsequent profit taking pulled it down again.
"The one percent from parity seems to be a strong anchor for the zloty which returned to it from below and above that level," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 0.99/0.95 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than yesterday's close at 0.75/0.72 percent. It closed at 3.2880/90 to the dollar, just up from 3.2885/95 on Tuesday and at 1.8775/85 to the mark, up from 1.8842/50.
"The zloty is now likely to stabilise at around this one- percent-above-parity peg," one dealer said.
On the money market O/N rates were flat at 22.80/23.30 percent throughout the day, while T/N rates eased 0.2 point to 22.75/23.30 percent.
Banks placed no bids at the central bank's 300 million zloty reverse repo tender.

The Polish finance ministry sold only four million zlotys worth of its 15-percent two-year bonds and rejected all bids for the 12-percent five-year bonds at today's one billion zloty tender on demand of 271 million zlotys.

"The low demand and bids for low prices are most likely a result of the recent uncertainty over whether Poland would sufficiently tighten its fiscal policy next year to avoid a Czech-style currency crisis," one senior analyst said.
Bids for the shorter paper totalled 195.1 million zlotys and for the longer bonds 76 million zlotys.
The minimum price for the two year bonds fell to 89.47 against 89.69 at the last auction on June 3, the average price fell to 89.61 against 89.81 and the maximum price was 89.70.
The Polish central bank has recently warned that if Poland did not balance its budget in 1998 the zloty might share the fate of the Czech crown due to a fast widening trade gap.
But the government has already said a balanced budget was out of the question and the finance ministry proposed a deficit of 1.9 percent next year against 2.8 percent planned for this year.
